prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S419: The Integrated Tactical Management Position is the primary workstation for real-time coordination of Meridian departure flow, arrival flow, airport capacity, and airspace constraints.
S420: It presents a combined tactical view so that the Regional Flow Manager can compare planned demand, measured throughput, and active control measures without changing applications.
S421: The Common Situation Display provides the base map, timeline, flight list, and measure status panels used at the position.
S422: The Regional Flow Platform synchronizes the tactical display with the Time Synchronization Service so that all timestamps, countdowns, and validity intervals use the same operational clock.
S423: The Arrival Regulation Console is also known as Nightjar at the Integrated Tactical Management Position, where the alias is displayed only in operator profile help text.
S424: Arrival demand is monitored against the Airport Acceptance Rate, current sequencing performance, and any Ground Delay Program that remains in effect.
S425: The Tower Supervisor uses the display to see runway assignment pressure, airborne sequence spacing, and expected crossing points at the North Runway Meter and the South Runway Meter.
S426: Emberline sends revised departure metering advisories when runway demand exceeds the configured queue threshold.
S427: Skylark must refresh the apron movement layer within five seconds of each validated surface event.
S428: The Slot Allocation Engine produces the Pushback Window Token when the agreed departure window is frozen for tactical execution.
S429: The Airport CDM Portal exposes agreed Target Off Block Time values and stakeholder remarks to the tactical position in read-only mode unless the operator has an assigned coordination role.
S430: The Demand Prediction Service continuously updates short-term traffic forecasts using the Flight Intent Message stream and recent airport performance history.
S431: The Capacity Assessment Module recalculates available capacity when runway configuration, weather category, staffing assumptions, or sector workload changes.
S432: The Airspace Sector Planner monitors sector demand through the Sector Load Monitor and confirms whether proposed measures are compatible with en route capacity.
S433: The Military Airspace Liaison can mark an airspace release or closure assumption for review before it affects tactical flow calculations.
S434: The Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies weather impacts shown from the Weather Ingest Gateway before the position applies weather-driven capacity values.
S435: The Airport Duty Manager can declare Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, or Contingency Fallback State from the tactical header after coordination is complete.
S436: When the operating state changes, the Business Rules Registry supplies the applicable thresholds for alerting, approval routing, and measure publication.
S437: The Airline Operations Coordinator and Aircraft Operator Representative review proposed timing changes in the same timeline used by flow staff, which reduces duplicate verbal coordination.
S438: The Ground Handling Dispatcher uses the Handling Resource Planner view to compare planned off-block demand with available servicing capacity at affected stands.
S439: The Gate Conflict Detector highlights stand conflicts that would undermine a proposed departure recovery plan or compress arrival unloading capacity.
S440: A Tactical Regulation Proposal can be drafted directly from the display, checked against current capacity assumptions, and routed through the Alert Distribution Hub for stakeholder acknowledgement.
S441: Accepted adjustments are reflected as Calculated Takeoff Time updates, Slot Compliance State changes, or airport capacity annotations depending on the measure type.
S442: Every operator action, system recommendation, acknowledgement, and rejected alternative is written to the Collaborative Decision Log and the Audit Event Ledger for traceability and post-operation analysis.
S443: Surface constraints are treated as tactical capacity inputs because they can change the feasible order, timing, and routing of aircraft after demand has already been balanced against airspace capacity.
S444: The Regional Flow Platform correlates surface equipment conditions with flight intent, stand assignment, and runway plan data before recommending any change to the active tactical plan.
S445: The Surface Surveillance Adapter provides current movement area occupancy and equipment status indicators to the Ramp Movement Board and the Tower Sequence Manager.
S446: When a gate bridge, ground power unit, fuel hydrant point, or marked taxilane is unavailable, the Ramp Control Lead verifies whether the condition blocks a single movement, a stand group, or a wider apron route.
S447: The Airport Duty Manager records the operational significance of the condition in the Airport CDM Portal so that all planning components use the same constraint description.
S448: The Capacity Assessment Module converts persistent surface constraints into reduced stand throughput, extended turn buffers, or modified taxi-out assumptions.
S449: Fuel vehicle holds affect the tactical plan by delaying off-block readiness even when crew, passengers, and aircraft serviceability are otherwise complete.
S450: Tower Sequence Manager uses the hold advice to prevent a departure from being sequenced ahead of a fueling constraint that is still active.
S451: The Airline Operations Coordinator remains responsible for confirming whether the affected flight should keep its Target Off Block Time, request a new value, or accept a later Calculated Takeoff Time.
S452: Airline Interface Adapter produces the Late Baggage Tag List when baggage reconciliation data indicates that departure readiness may be overstated.
